posts.text: A primary catalyst for Lords Chloro’s superior Q1 margins appears to be strong price realization in Chlorinated Paraffin Wax (CPW), which forms its largest revenue stream after Caustic Soda. In contrast, TGV SRAAC’s margins were weighed down by falling realizations in Chloromethanes (MDC and Chloroform), which represent its primary secondary revenue contributor.

posts.text: Very true. I firmly believe this scrip to be undervalued. With the present capacity and near term expanded capacity taken into consideration, it is damn cheap from whatever angle you want to judge it, management capability, capacity build up, shareholders value addition , integrity of management, financial ratios, gross and net profit etc. If they can be little more shareholder friendly by way of con call, higher dividend, then market value can go up drastically.

posts.author: lohiyaakshay08
posts.community: TGV SRAAC erstwhile Sree Rayalseema Alkali
posts.text: image 1003×366 23 KB A decent quarter, with sales up 11% and PAT up 17%. The 5 MW solar plant was only completed in late June / early July, so none of that benefit shows up in Q1 numbers. It should start contributing from Q2. On the larger programme, the 450 TPD caustic soda expansion, remaining 37.7 MW of solar and the 50 MW BESS are all slated for completion in Q4FY27. So I’d expect Q2 and Q3 to print healthy growth on the existing base, while Q4 could look optically weak — interest, depreciation and operating costs from the new assets all hit the P&L before the capacity has had a chance to…
